readings.content: Through the enumeration of the Grail's enticements and torments winds the sorrowful history of the Witches of the Dry Land: the ordeal of birth from two wombs, their struggle from and supplication of the Grail, the yearning for union which drives them all.

readings_cn.intro: “聖杯的誘惑之數多於其苦痛，但苦痛才是它的真本性。生誕是第一苦痛，而干渴是第七苦痛。”
readings_cn.content: 要列举杯的诱惑与苦痛，离不开“干涸之地两女巫”哀伤的历史：降生于两个子宫的煎熬，摆脱杯的挣扎与对杯的乞求，对结合为一的共同渴盼。

items.name: A True and Accurate History of the Shadowless Kings
items.description: 'A True and Accurate History of the Shadowless Kings, by Isaac of Karth.' Isaac describes the thousand-year ascendancy of the Shadowless Empire.
items.description_cn: 《真实准确的无影众王史，卡斯的艾萨克著》。艾萨克在本书中描写了无影帝国持续千年的霸权。

readings.intro: 'The first and greatest history' is described herein. The Persian Empire - 'the sons of Achaemenes', 'the Shadowless Kings', 'the most Glorious Empire' - survives the assaults of Alexander the Great and flourishes as late as the fifth century.
readings.content: After the fall of Rome, the Shadowless Empire takes Byzantium under its wing, and moves East against the Land of the Great River. Isaac begins to recount the invasion struggling against 'the unskinned armies of the hooded serpents', but ends abruptly with a series of incantations that he claims allowed the Shadowless Empire to persist.

readings_cn.intro: 本书描述了“第一重亦最伟大的历史”。波斯帝国——又称“阿契美尼斯的子嗣”、“无影众王”、“最辉煌帝国”——挺过了亚历山大大帝的强攻，繁荣昌盛直至第五世纪。
readings_cn.content: 罗马陷落后，无影帝国将拜占庭置于自己的荫蔽下，并东进攻取大河流域。作者艾萨克的叙述以对抗“由扁颈蛇组成的无肤之师”的侵略战争开始，却又唐突地以一系列他称能令无影帝国存续的祷文收尾。

items.name: The High Mysteries of the Innermost Chamber of our Church Solar
items.name_cn: 《吾太阳神教核心厅室之极密》
items.description: 'The High Mysteries of the Innermost Chamber of our Church Solar'. Secret rites of the Church of the Unconquered Sun, which held power in at least two Histories.
items.description_cn: 《吾太阳神教核心厅室之极密》。本书记载了无敌太阳教会的秘密仪式，该教至少在两重历史上掌握过权势。

readings.intro: The Church chiefly worshipped the Sun-in-Splendour, the original undivided sun; but this text also includes the devotions of its aspects as the chilly winter dawn and the departing sunset, as well as the Meniscate, the Sun's 'night-self'. Priests of the Church were all male, but rites are also included which allowed women to cross ceremonially to manhood.
readings.content: The Church's highest rites were performed in the Concursum, the chamber at the Mansus' heart where the Hours were known to pass. These rites include salutations to non-solar Hours: the Grail, the Ring-Yew, the Horned Axe and the Thunderskin.

readings_cn.intro: 该教派崇拜的主要对象是骄阳，即原初的，未分裂的太阳；但本书也记载了如何祀奉骄阳的其他面相：祀奉冷冽的冬季黎明、消逝的夕阳、还有弧月，即太阳的“夜间自我”。该教派的祭司均为男性，但书中也记载了令女人转性而具备男人特质的仪式。
readings_cn.content: 该教派将最重要的仪式放在聚点举行；聚点是位于漫宿核心的厅室，已知的司辰行经之处。此类仪式包含致敬与太阳无关的司辰——圣杯、环杉、双角利斧、轰雷之皮——的环节。

items.name: Medusa's Lament
items.description: On the death of the Hour called Seven-Coils, 'the Father of the Mother'.
items.description_cn: 描写了名为七蟠的司辰，又称“母亲之父”的死亡。

readings.intro: The first part of the poem describes the ambush of the Seven-Coils by a warrior 'scarred all over by the traitor gods, scarred even unto his eyes, so that the sight of the great coils would not destroy him'.
readings.content: The battle rages on until the Seven-Coils drowns in its own blood, at which point the narrative turns mystical and allusive. A seven-titled goddess arises from the foam of its blood: she is an armoured queen, a serpent-daughter, a key, a healer, a murderess, an oracle, but her seventh title is not to be revealed.

readings_cn.intro: 诗的第一部分描述了七蟠遭遇一名战士的伏击，此人“全身上下都是那些背信弃义的神留下的伤疤，连双目上都是，所以他不会因目睹虬结的蟠身而毁灭。”
readings_cn.content: 激战一直持续至七蟠溺毙在自己的鲜血中，诗风由此转向神秘而委婉。拥有七项头衔的女神从七蟠的血沫中升起：她是披坚执锐的女王，是蛇的女儿，是钥匙，是治疗者，是杀人者，是神谕祭司，但她的第七头衔隐而不宣。

items.name: The Book of Masks
items.description: Athena Vana's work on the rogue Hour called the Vagabond, who is also known as the Laughingthrush, the Centipede, the Pilgrim, and by many other names - or as Vana has it, 'masks'.
items.description_cn: 雅典娜·凡娜对被名为浪游旅人的流浪司辰的研究手记；此司辰还有“笑鸫”、“蜈蚣”、“巡礼者”等许多别称——或依凡纳的说法，“面具”。

readings.intro: The Mask of the Laughingthrush, says Athena Vana, had a great friendship with the Sun-in-Splendour, the highmost Hour of the Mansus (now divided and departed). The Mask of the Sight-Thief painted the river in the Mansus. The Mask of the Vagabond was forbidden the Mansus, not for what she had done, but for what would occur...
readings.content: The Mask of the Centipede recalled her birth-place, Miah, which had punished her for creeping into the temple precinct. This Mask cursed Miah to drink only dust and to be remembered only by the wind - 'for not beneath any Mask does she forgive, and the Centipede's hunger is not to be forgotten.'

readings_cn.intro: 笑鸫的面具，据雅典娜·凡纳说，与漫宿的至尊之司辰骄阳（如今已分裂消逝）交情甚笃。景象窃贼的面具在漫宿画下河流。浪游旅人的面具在漫宿是为禁忌，原因不是她已做过的事，而是她会引发的事……
readings_cn.content: 蜈蚣的面具代表了她的生身地——弥阿城，曾因她爬进神殿域而对她降下刑罚。这副面具诅咒弥阿只能饮啜沙尘，在风中消逝无闻——“她并不因隐于面具之后而饶恕仇敌，蜈蚣的饥渴总有一天要得到满足。”

items.name: In The Mountains...
items.description: 'In The Mountains As Upon The Plain There May Not Be A Path Where None Has Passed'. Ninegala of Lagash describes the secrets to be found in mountains.
items.description_cn: 《山中亦如平川，许无前人未达之途》。拉格什的宁娜伽勒在本书中描述了山中有待发现的秘密。

readings.intro: Ninegala tells a number of lively stories about riddling ogres and wars between mountain tribes, but turns sombre in the tale of the Empty-Handed Hunter: a lover of the Grail who sought to match her appetites and join her as an Hour, but in the end rent and devoured himself, giving his name to the mountains he had once roamed.
readings.content: Ninegala claims that the Hours who sometimes manifest as birds - the Laughingthrush, the Ivory Dove, the Beachcrow and the Witch-and-Sister - meet at a secret location on a mountaintop to exchange gossip unheard by their peers. Now and then a mortal overhears them. The mortal is always obliterated, and the meeting-place always changed.

readings_cn.intro: 作者宁娜伽勒在书中讲述了几个热闹的故事，有关于说谜语的食人魔的，也有关于山中部落间的战争的，但在讲述空手猎人传说时，故事基调转向忧郁：圣杯有一位情人，他想要符合她的胃口，成为与她并肩的司辰，最终却撕开并吞吃了自身，将名字留给了他曾漫游过的山脉。
readings_cn.content: 宁娜伽勒称那些有时以鸟型显现的司辰——笑鸫、骨白鸽、拾滩鸦和双生巫女——会在山顶的秘密地点会面，交换同僚没听过的闲话。时不时会有凡人不巧听见他们。这样的人总会被抹消，会面的地点也总在变化。

items.name: In Memory of Gods
items.description: 'The Barrowchild', a nameless Gaulish adept who joined an organisation identified as the Ordo Limiae, writes regretfully of the destruction of the gods-who-were-stone - the Hours who preceded humanity.
items.description_cn: 作者是一个无名的高卢人学徒“坟茔之子”，属于名为利米亚教团的组织。此人带着遗憾之情讲述了先于人类的司辰——石源诸神的毁灭。

readings.intro: The Barrowchild singles out the Scarred Tribune, the Red Grail, the Forge and the Moth for especial condemnation as murderers of the first gods. 'We live in the shadow of their crime', she writes, 'and we must evade it or repeat it.'
readings.content: The Barrowchild describes how the Grail drained the Hour called Tide, how the Moth 'usurped the Wheel from within', stealing its skin, and how the Forge first eclipsed then shattered Flint. 'Perhaps these are glories,' she observes, 'but then it cannot be that Glory is merciful.'

readings_cn.intro: 坟茔之子在书中着重点名谴责了伤疤护民官、赤杯、铸炉和飞蛾，因他们谋杀了最初的诸神。“我们活在他们罪行的阴影下，”她写到，“我们若不留心避免，必将重蹈覆辙。”
readings_cn.content: 坟茔之子描述了赤杯如何饮干名为浪潮的司辰，飞蛾如何“从内部篡夺转轮”，盗走了它的皮肤，以及铸炉如何先盖过燧石的光芒而后粉碎之。“也许这些行为可说是光辉的，”她评论到，“然而辉光不可说是仁慈的。”

items.name: The Sevenfold Slaying of the Seven-Coiled
items.description: An account of the destruction of a primaeval Hour, a god-who-was-Stone.
items.description_cn: 记录了远古司辰——一位石源神的毁灭。

readings.intro: There are twelve verses. In the first, an ascendant Hour identified as the Scarred One enumerates his justifications for destroying the Seven-Coiled: its appetites, its growth, its enmity to humanity. In the second, a priestess puts out his eyes and scars his skin to protect him against the Seven-Coiled's magics. In each of the next seven verses, he destroys one aspect of the Seven-Coiled...
readings.content: In the tenth verse, the Scarred One bathes his priestess-patron in the blood of the Seven-Coiled, to lend her power. In the eleventh, they assault the 'temple behind the world', entering it by force. In the twelfth, they swear a tripartite oath to protect their ancestors, their descendants, and themselves.

readings_cn.intro: 共十二节。在第一节，一位飞生而来，称为伤疤者的司辰为他消灭七蟠而辩解，列举了种种理由：七蟠的口腹之欲，它的不断成长，它对人类的敌意。在第二节，一名女祭司熄灭了他的眼，并在他皮肤上刻下伤疤，以此保护他免受七蟠魔法的伤害。在接下来的七节，他每一节消灭七蟠的一个面相……
readings_cn.content: 在第十节，伤疤者将七蟠的鲜血洒遍庇护他的女祭司全身，以此借给她神力。在第十一节，他们向“隐于世后的庙宇”发动袭击，强行进入其内。在第十二节，他们许下三重誓言，将其先祖、其后裔、其自身保护起来。

items.name: My Deeds, My Powers, My Achievements...
items.name_cn: 《我的事迹、我的力量、我的成就……》
items.description: 'My Deeds, My Powers, My Achievements and the Injustices Perpetrated Against Me'. Hokobald of Pocsind, formerly of the order of immortals called by some the House of Lethe, settles scores.
items.description_cn: 《我的事迹、我的力量、我的成就和我所面临的不公》。波辛德的霍科博尔德——被有些人称为“遗忘家族”的不死者教团的前成员——在本书中反击了该教团。

readings.intro: Hokobald boasts of his royal descent, and insists that the magics of the Forge are more effective when practised by those of noble blood.
readings.content: Pocsind complains of his condemnation by the Ordo Limiae. He acknowledges that he has 'undergone alterations' after the 'consummation of that particular delight', but insists that these changes are both elegant and inevitable. 'Who is the fire, and who the fuel?' he asks rhetorically.

readings_cn.intro: 霍科博尔德吹嘘自己的皇室血统，并坚称铸炉的魔法在由血统高贵之人施行时更有效。
readings_cn.content: 波辛德埋怨利米亚教团给他定罪。他承认在“达成那种特定的愉悦”后，他“有所改变”，但他坚称此类改变既是高雅，也是必然的。“究竟谁是火，谁是燃料？”他诘问道。

items.name: The Dream of the Conspiracy of the Lower Skies
items.description: The disgraced oracle Damaon Azenaten sifts through the tall tales of Penelope of Gordion, the work of the court poet Kalle and the forbidden fragments of the work of the adept Arrettrez, identifying common themes.
items.description_cn: 由名声扫地的神谕者达马翁·阿谮那滕筛选收集而成，素材源自戈尔迪翁的佩涅罗佩所写的天方夜谭，宫廷诗人凯勒的作品，还有学徒阿雷特雷兹著作中遭禁的片段。

readings.intro: Damaon insists that the Hours, far more than mortals, are subject to their passions - to hatred, and even to love. 'The seasons of famine and plenty, the turn of the Earth, the transformations of the furnace - all these are only the results of the enactment of the lesser passions of the Hours.'
readings.content: Damaon suggests that the Hours have constrained their rivalry to avoid a war within the House of the Sun. He identifies the 'Fear of the Crime of the Sky' as the reason that Hours do not satisfy other passions. He speculates on the horrifying possibility of Hours turned alukite. 'What then would they devour?'

readings_cn.intro: 达马翁坚称司辰也屈从于自己的激情——屈从于憎恨，甚至爱，其程度远超凡人。“年景的好坏，地球的转动，熔炉的转变——所有这些仅仅只是司辰的激情中较弱的那些成就的结果。”
readings_cn.content: 达马翁认为众司辰已然收敛对立，以免在太阳的居屋引发战争。他发觉司辰不去追求其他激情的原因是“惧怕天孽”。他推断司辰存在吸血阿卢卡化的可怕可能性。“那样的话他们会吞噬什么呢？”

items.name: The Book of the White Cat
items.description: Stories brought to Penelope of Gordion by a blind white cat.
items.description_cn: 由一只瞎眼白猫传递给戈尔迪翁的佩涅罗佩的故事。

readings.intro: The aviform Hours - the Crow, the Laughingthrush, the Dove, and the twin Kites - have been known to meet in the mountains north of Gordion, at a place called the Roost, to exchange gossip. Penelope indicates that mortals who hear their words directly are obliterated, but claims that her cat goes unnoticed and returns to her with rumours from the Hours' meetings.
readings.content: The stories that Penelope claims as Hour-gossip are fragmentary and confusing: accounts of contests where Hope and Dread and the Shadowless Empire are used as game-pieces, agendas of ruin and remembrance from no known history. The most interesting element is the protective incantation she records at the end of the book, after she worries that the Hours might in fact learn of her spying.

readings_cn.intro: 已知鸟型司辰——乌鸦、笑鸫、白鸽、还有孪鸢——会在戈尔迪翁北部的山中一个叫做栖木的地方见面，互聊闲话。佩涅罗佩称直接听到他们话语的凡人会被抹消掉，但她的猫不被神查知地回到她身边，告诉了她从司辰集会听来的传闻。
readings_cn.content: 佩内洛普所述的司辰间的闲话既零碎又混乱：有以希望、恐惧与无影帝国为棋子相互竞夺的经过，有来自不为人知的历史的关于残迹与铭记的纲领。最有趣的是她担心众司辰会发现她打探神机，所以在书的结尾收录了保护祷文。

items.name: The Focus of Amber
items.description: Omar, the Blaze, spent seven years manning a lighthouse in Tyre, in atonement for the extinguishing of a sacred flame. By the end of his stint, he was so terrified of fire that he could not stand to share a room with a candle. This work was written in partial penance.
items.description_cn: 奥马尔，又名“炽焰”，为了清偿自己熄灭圣焰的罪过，在推罗看了七年灯塔。而在这场苦役最后，他对火焰产生了莫大的恐惧，甚至无法与烛焰共处一室。写这本书是他苦修的一部分。

readings.intro: Omar claims that the Hour called Watchman is both a god-who-was-flesh - an Hour who was mortal - and also a god-from-Light - an Hour who descended from the Glory - but adds, finally, that the Watchman's origin is triple, and that 'in essence, he is Amber.'
readings.content: The Watchman, according to Omar, was once another Hour entirely, who ascended into the Glory to escape efforts by other Hours to send him to Nowhere. It may be that Omar's sense of persecution creeps into the narrative at this point: certainly it grows less coherent, and the last part is devoted to attempts to prove that eyes, eggs and the Sun are all in some sense conjunct.

readings_cn.intro: 奥马尔声称名为守夜人的司辰既是肉源神——原为凡人的司辰——也是光源神——降自辉光的司辰——但在最后又补充说，守夜人有三重来源，即是说“实质上，他是琥珀神”。
readings_cn.content: 守夜人，据奥马尔称，原先完全是另外一位司辰，因其他司辰欲将其赶进虚界而逃入辉光，升入其间。奥马尔讲到这点时可能渗入了他自己的偏见：可想而知，此处的行文变得不那么连贯。书的最后一部分致力于证明眼瞳，卵和太阳在某种意义上是一体的。

items.name: The Songs of the Carapace Cross
items.description: Micah Xi, sometimes called the Magus of Quartz, etched this work in acid on stone. It has been reproduced many times since, but the reproductions are often lost to landslides.
items.description_cn: 米卡·席，有时也称“石英术士”，用酸液将本作蚀刻在了石头上。本作后被多次复制，不过复制品往往散佚于山体滑坡。

readings.intro: Xi describes the rites of the gods-who-were-stone, the first Hours, as practiced before the existence of human civilisation by the 'Carapace Cross'. He claims a final survivor of the Cross shared the information with him.
readings.content: The rites are largely obsolete now. Few have been observed, in the last thousand years at least, to have any effect at all. Nevertheless, Xi identifies at least one invocation of particular power. He warns that it should be used with caution, lest the gods-who-were-stone might find their way back from Nowhere.

readings_cn.intro: 作者席描述了人类文明存在之前，“介壳种”所施行的最初的司辰——石源诸神的仪式。他称这些信息是最后一名存活的介壳种告诉他的。
readings_cn.content: 这些仪式现已大半遭到淘汰。至少在过去的一千年里，其中绝大多数都没显出任何作用。不过，席确认了至少一个拥有某种法力的祷文。他警告说此祷文须得谨慎使用，以免石源神找到从虚界返回的道路。

items.name: The Origins of Hours
items.description: The sage and ecstatic Soham, a frequent visitor to the Mansus, claimed to have discoursed with the Beachcrow in person. Soham later insisted on a sky-burial.
items.description_cn: 漫宿的常客，睿智而又痴狂的索哈姆宣称自己与拾滩鸦当面对谈过。索哈姆随后坚决要求自己死后执行天葬。

readings.intro: Soham's writings veer from poetry to confession. He identifies gods from flesh (those who were mortal), from blood (those who arose from sacrifice), from Light (entry from the Glory) and from stone (those who arose before his knowledge.) He insists that the Moth was the first god-who-was-blood, but later contradicts himself and claims it was the Red Grail.
readings.content: 'The Mansus was different before the first god came from Light, but never doubt it existed, even then.'

readings_cn.intro: 索哈姆的文字由抒情转为自白。他将神分为肉源（原为凡人）、血源（经献祭升为）、光源（从辉光而来）和石源（早于他所知）的。他强调飞蛾为首位血源神，后却又自相矛盾地称赤杯才是首位。
readings_cn.content: “第一位神明自光中到来时，漫宿并非现在的模样，但无需怀疑彼时它既已存在。”

items.name: Where Has She Gone?
items.description: 'The Speeth' - perhaps a single adept, perhaps a council of scholars - hypothesises secret events from limited evidence with persuasive accuracy.
items.description_cn: “斯佩斯”——或许是某个学徒，或许是某个学者结社——根据有限的证据推测出了一些秘密事件，其准确度颇为可信。

readings.intro: The Vagabond is recorded to have travelled not only the Mansus and the Wood, not only all nine continents, but also places forbidden to other Hours...
readings.content: From Hour-gossip and invisible lore, Speeth deduces that the Vagabond has visited Nowhere, but that she will not return. He also asserts that she has yet to visit the Glory, but that inevitably, this must be her goal.

readings_cn.intro: 据记载，浪游旅人不仅旅经漫宿和林地，游遍全部九个大陆，还去过那些禁止其他司辰踏足的地方……
readings_cn.content: 通过司辰间的闲话和无形的密传，斯佩斯推断浪游旅人造访过虚界，但不会再去。他还宣称她尚未造访过辉光，但或早或晚，她必然会去。

items.name: The Book of the Extinguished Heart
items.description: In the days of the Shadowless Kings, Ennis Lazali was executed for prophesying the Division of the Sun. If any of his captors grew Long, they probably feel rather abashed now.
items.description_cn: 在无影众王时代，恩尼斯·拉扎里因预言太阳的分裂而被处以极刑。若抓捕他的人日后长成了长生者，现在大概会感到惭愧。

readings.intro: Lazali indicates that the Sun will be divided in the Malleary, by the Forge of Days, armed with the love in her heart.
readings.content: 'Love will not be the cause of the Sun's death, but rather envy. Envy will not be the cause of the Sun's death, but rather thirst. Thirst shall not be the cause of his death, but curiosity. Curiosity shall not be his end; rather will it be love.'

readings_cn.intro: 拉扎里称太阳将在锤炼场被白日铸炉分裂，后者的凶器是心中的爱。
readings_cn.content: “导致太阳之死的不会是爱，而是妒忌。导致太阳之死的不会是妒忌，而是渴求。导致太阳之死必不是渴求，而是好奇。置他于死地的必不是好奇，终究还是爱。”

items.name: How the End will Begin
items.description: A prophecy of the Wars of the Roads, recorded in the Subcontinent in the days before the Great Hooded Princes.
items.description_cn: 关于路权战争的预言，记录于兜颈贵胄还未出现时的次大陆。

readings.intro: In the foretold war, the Children of the Leashed Flame march on the cities of the Continent, but the 'Enactors of Solar Law' and the 'Triple Sisterhood' join forces to hold them back... at tremendous cost.
readings.content: 'In that battle between the Imperishable Legions and the Leashed Flame, the Legions will perish and the Flame will be unleashed.'

readings_cn.intro: 在预言所述的战争中，受控之火的子女向大陆上的城邦进军，但“太阳法的制定者”和“三倍姐妹会”联合起来击退了他们……在付出巨大代价后。
readings_cn.content: “在不灭军团与受控之火的战斗中，军团将灭亡而火将解除控制。”

items.name: The Manner in which the Alchemist was Spared
items.description: In 1782, Anaël Verdier used this text as the basis for a presentation to the Academy of Sciences in Paris. He was executed in secret the following morning without trial.
items.description_cn: 1782年，阿纳尔·维迪尔以本书为据在巴黎科学院进行了宣讲。他于次日清晨被不经审判直接处决。

readings.intro: In the days of the Carapace Cross, when humanity lived in the dark and ate on its knees, humans could enter the Mansus like vermin. One learnt the arts of Flint, the arts of shaping and remaking...
readings.content: 'Through the Black, the Yellow, the Red, the Unwise Mortal ascended to the shadow of the Egg Unhatching, and remained in his service. He may be there to this day.'

readings_cn.intro: 在介壳种时代，人类生活在黑暗里，跪着吃东西；那时的人类可以像寄生虫一样进入漫宿。有一人学会了燧石的技法，即塑形与再造的技法……
readings_cn.content: “经过黑，黄，红，这名愚蠢的凡人升入逆孵之卵的阴影，并加入侍奉他的行列。他或许时至今日仍在那里。”

items.name: Five Creations
items.description: The itinerant scholar Shohei debated five possible origins for humanity with a hooded figure since claimed to be the Beach-Crow. Shohei later claimed that all these accounts had proven false, but the debate was, nevertheless, recorded.
items.description_cn: 游学者肖黑在本书中讨论了五种人类可能的起源，并佐以一个蒙面的，他称之为“拾滩鸦”的形象。肖黑之后又称这些描述已全部被证伪，但无论如何，讨论本身还是被记录了下来。

readings.intro: 'THE CARAPACE ORIGIN: we were born from shell, like the children of the wasp from the spider. THE GLORIOUS ORIGIN: our life-motes descended from Light. THE ORIGIN BEFOULED: we were found naked and smeared with muck in the roots of the Wood...'
readings.content: Shohei's preferred theories are that we are the children of apes who walked upright, although his tone here is satirical; or that we consumed not only our parents, 'which is not the Crime of the Sky', but also our origin, so that we came from Nowhere.

readings_cn.intro: “介壳源：我们诞自甲壳，如同黄蜂的孩子从蜘蛛体内钻出。辉源：我们生命的微粒降自“光”。受污之源：我们出世时浑身赤裸，身上沾着林地根部的淤泥……”
readings_cn.content: 肖黑偏爱的理论是：我们是直立行走的猿猴的子孙，尽管他说及此论时语带讥讽；又或者我们不仅摄食了我们的父母，“此行并非天孽”，也摄食了我们的起源，所以我们来自虚界。

items.name: Commandments For the Preservation of All That Exists
items.name_cn: 《关于维持一切事物存续的教令》
items.description: Black Elie, Damascene Matriarch of the Sisterhood of the Knot, was imprisoned by the emperor Didius Julianus. She reportedly instructed that these secret doctrines be recorded in writing to preserve against their loss. Regrettably, the story goes, Didius Julianus ordered that the work be entombed with her in an unmarked sepulcher.
items.description_cn: 大马士革绳结姐妹会的头领“黑色”艾丽遭到了皇帝狄第乌斯·尤利安努斯囚禁。据记载，她曾命人将这些秘密教义记录成书，以保其免于遗失，永远存续。遗憾的是，据传说狄第乌斯·尤利安努斯命人将本作随她葬入了一个没有标记的墓室。

readings.intro: Elie describes powerful protective incantations to be used in a variety of circumstances.
readings.content: 'It is essential that these Protections be completed every fourth year, to defend against the entry of the Worms and against the avidity of the Wave and the Wound.' In the current History at least, there is no indication that these Protections have been performed regularly for at least the last thousand years.

readings_cn.intro: 艾丽在本书中描述了能用于各种情况的强大保护咒。
readings_cn.content: “重要的是，这些保护咒需每四年补修一次，以抵御蠕虫进入以及‘水波’和‘创口’的热盼。”至少在现今这重历史中，过去至少一千年内没有迹象表明有人定期施放过这些保护咒。

items.name: The Time of Division
items.description: In which Amira Zahra prophesies the events later known as the Intercalate, when the Hour called Sun-in-Splendour will be divided.
items.description_cn: 阿米拉·扎拉在本书中预言了后人称为“置闰”的事件：名为骄阳的司辰被分裂。

readings.intro: 'The Sun will be divided that it might not sire children. Still its children shall be Four in number and its children shall be Seven in number and its children shall also be Numberless. The Numberless shall open the way for the Seven, and the Seven shall consume the Four...'
readings.content: Amira prophesies four great wars before the Second Dawn, when the Sun-in-Splendour shall rise again. She cautions: 'Sunrise is blood, and I foretell now that the Sun shall rise from blood, yet not the colour of the blood, nor the hour of Night.' She includes a rite that she speculates will be necessary for the Second Dawn.

readings_cn.intro: 太阳将遭分裂，故它许不能再生产子嗣。即便如此，其子嗣之数应为四再其子嗣之数应为七再其子嗣之数更应不可计数。不可计数者将为七者打开道路，七者将摄食四者……
readings_cn.content: 阿米拉预卜了“第二拂晓”前，即骄阳再度升起前的四场大战。她提醒道：“日出为血，我于此预言骄阳将从血中升起，却既无鲜血的颜色，亦非夜晚的时辰。”她给出了她推测第二拂晓所需的一个仪式。

items.name: A Manual for Departure
items.description: The author, who identifies itself as the Jekadu, claims to be one of the Great Hooded Princes of the Land of the River. The style is informal, even chatty.
items.description_cn: 作者自称杰卡杜，为圣河流域的兜颈贵胄之一。文风并不正式，甚至可说像闲聊。

readings.intro: 'No, these doors shouldn't be recorded, but if we had only recorded things before we'd had to leave the Fifth History, we would be in a much better state. So here I am writing it down, and if you don't like it you can sanction me.'
readings.content: The 'Manual for Departure' lists a number of strategies - occult, martial and political - for quick escapes. Many are irrelevant, obsolete or enigmatic, but the Manual does include a number of powerful techniques for opening portals.

readings_cn.intro: 不，不应该记录这些门，但如果那时，我们在被迫离开第五史前做了记录，我们现在的景况会好得多。所以我现在将其付诸笔端，如果你不喜欢，你可以制裁我。
readings_cn.content: 《脱身手册》列举了若干——密教上，军事上和政治上的——快速脱逃策略。其中许多是可有可无，过时落后或高深难懂的，但这本手册的确给出了若干强力的开启门洞的技术。

items.name: Inaam, Kapigiginlupir, Garkie, Cryppys
items.name_cn: 《伊纳姆、卡皮吉吉努皮尔、加尔基、克雷皮斯》
items.description: In which four enigmatic figures tell the stories they've heard over the years at the Roost, the secret location where the aviform Hours congregate.
items.description_cn: 书中的四个神秘人物讲述了他们多年来在“栖木”——鸟型司辰的集会地——听到的故事。

readings.intro: INAAM: Has not the Beach-Crow shared his treasures? GARKIE: Not the rarest. He takes those things most precious, which he claims found, not stolen.
readings.content: The Beach-Crow, Kapigiginlupir suggests, is not only a thief, but also a spy and even a voyeur. He has hidden the memory of secret couplings among the Hours and their Names in the corners of the House, as treasures to gloat over. There is particularly fevered speculation on a liaison between the Ring-Yew, that fervent Hour of the Wood, and the Mare-in-the-Tree, who sometimes has been the Witch's Sister.

readings_cn.intro: 伊纳姆：拾滩鸦没有分享他的宝藏吗？加尔基：没有分享最稀有的。他把最珍贵的留给自己了，号称那些是他找到的，不是偷来的。
readings_cn.content: 卡皮吉吉努皮尔认为拾滩鸦不仅是盗贼，同时也是探子，甚至喜欢窥淫。他把司辰和祂们的具名者间秘密交合的记忆藏在居屋的角落，作为暗中夸耀的宝藏。还有一个很火的猜测：热情如火的林地司辰环杉，和有时与女巫做姐妹的树中牝马，这两者间有私情。

items.name: The Voyages of Ferninshun of Oreol
items.description: A travelogue of sorts.
items.description_cn: 一本类似游记的书。

readings.intro: Ferninshun clearly visited the Mansus, sailing the length of the Painted River. He also claims to have traversed a sea of finest sand, to have dared the blazing waves of the Sun's surface, and to have descended to an underworld ocean lit by lamps of black nephrite...
readings.content: Ferninshun's final voyage is to retirement on a peaceful island across an evening sea, where he identifies a spring whose waters will keep him safe. 'I will be forgotten,' he declares, 'and this work my only trace.'

readings_cn.intro: 斐宁舜显然在沿画中之河航行时拜访过漫宿。他还称他横渡过沙滩最细腻的海域，挑战过太阳表面的热浪，也曾下潜到由墨玉照亮的地底之海……
readings_cn.content: 在最后一次远航中，斐宁舜跨越了薄暮的海面，到一座平静的岛屿上安度余生。他认为那里有一眼能保证他的安全的泉水。“人们会忘记我，”他宣告说，“而这本书是我留下的唯一痕迹。”

items.name: The Scar in the Sky
items.description: Nyn wrote this, and came to regret it.
items.description_cn: 作者宁在写下本书后追悔不迭。

readings.intro: Each page of this book contains one word only, but as each page is turned, a knowledge creeps in.
readings.content: The final page is crowded. Each reader of the book records the same word. Now it is my turn.

readings_cn.intro: 这本书每一页只写有一个词，但每翻过一页，便有一个知识潜入脑中。
readings_cn.content: 最后一页写得满满当当。书的每个读者都会在此处记下同一个词。现在轮到我了。

items.name: Kitling Ripe and the Moldywarp's Grave (and Other Stories)
items.name_cn: 《老成仔猫与鼹鼠的坟墓（及其他故事）》
items.description: A lusciously illustrated tome of loosely connected children's stories, collected by one N.K. Field. Few of them are remotely suitable for children.
items.description_cn: 一本插图华美的大书，内含数篇关联松散的儿童故事，由署名N·K·菲尔德之人收集成册。里面没有几个故事适合儿童阅读。

readings.intro: The protagonist, a speechless cat-thing called Kitling Ripe, performs a series of elaborate rites to rescue members of her extended family, culminating in the resurrection of her 'other grandmother', Moldywarp.
readings.content: 'When the Snake-Witch killed the stag, Kitling snatched one of its eyes. When the Dry-Witch killed the sow, Kitling stole a cup of its blood. Then she took them to the place Moldywarp lay buried, and she shook out her hair, and she began to dance...'

readings_cn.intro: 本书主角，一只名为老成仔猫的无言猫形生物施行了一系列复杂的仪式来拯救她族中的亲属。在故事最后一幕，她复活了她的“另一位祖母”——鼹鼠。
readings_cn.content: “蛇女巫杀死牡鹿时，仔猫抠出了它一只眼睛。干涸女巫杀死牝猪时，仔猫偷去了它一杯血液。随后她带着这些东西到埋葬鼹鼠的地方，散开自己的头发，开始舞蹈……”

items.name: Rapt in the King
items.description: Detailed accounts by James Colin Murphy of secret bacchanals and ecstatic dances observed in necropolises and graveyards in Southern Europe, in Egypt and in Anatolia. The author is a self-confessed ghoul, an eater of buried flesh: he claims to have witnessed the dances while at his feasting.
items.description_cn: 詹姆斯·科林·墨菲在本书中详细记录了他在南欧、埃及和安纳托利亚的坟场与墓地中看到的秘密欢宴和迷醉之舞。作者其人坦白了自己是食尸鬼，啃食土中尸体的生物：他称他在大快朵颐时见到了书中的舞蹈。

readings.intro: The dances draw from the traditions of the Mysteries, of the cults of Isis and of Cybele, but include both symbolic and literal flayings, and the human heart is always central in the rites. The author punctuates his accounts with queasily sensuous descriptions of his own interrupted feasts.
readings.content: 'At these greater Feasts a Black Pig is always crowned as King before its Slaying. On this Occasion, its Heart was weighed in the Balance against a Knot of Feathers, and its Skin became a Cape for the Officiant. Its Flesh was left for the Crows, but I must confess my Interest was not in its Carcass but in the Perfumed Flesh of the Milliner laid fresh in the Earth.'

readings_cn.intro: 这套舞蹈源自祭奉女神伊西斯与库柏勒的密教所传承的奥秘，不仅含有象征和实际意义上的剥皮行为，而且永远以人类心脏为仪式的主轴。作者着重圈点了他对自己被打断的宴席的令人作呕的感官描写。
readings_cn.content: “在那些盛大宴席間，總有一頭黑豬在經受屠宰前被加冕為王。每逢此時，它的心髒會經天平與一片羽毛互較輕重，而它的皮會成為主祭的披風。它的血肉被留給烏鴉，但我必須坦白我意不在其屍骸，而在於女帽制造者新入土的噴了香水的肉體。”

items.name: The Viennese Conundra
items.description: Nico Van Driel describes odd events in Vienna - the disappearance of children; epidemics of parasite activity; animal mutilations; nightmares of worms; the activities of a charitable organisation, the New Ligeians, that funds the burial of the poor. She proposes peculiar connections between these activities.
items.description_cn: 妮可·梵·德里尔描述了维也纳发生的怪事——儿童消失、寄生虫大肆传染、动物被切掉肢体、关于蠕虫的噩梦、一个为穷人提供丧葬费，名为“新生丽姬亚”的慈善组织。她指出了这些现象间怪异的联系。

readings.intro: 'When the individual K. attends the meetings, black dogs are sacrificed and quartered. When the individual M. is in attendance, black mares are found with their throats slashed. I propose that these sacrifices are not necessary, but that our Ligeian friends may consider them 'fitting'. Herewith diagrams of the mutilations -'
readings.content: 'Medusa's Riddle, then, I choose to render as 'What is Not Seen?' There is another riddle, one I have heard rendered as 'What may be Lost?' I will delineate some historic attempts to answer it- these are in themselves, in some sense, sacrifices - '

readings_cn.intro: “K氏参加会议时，黑犬们被献祭并分为四块。M氏出席时，黑牝马们遭到割喉。我的意见是这些献祭是不必要的，但我们的丽姬亚朋友或许认为它们是‘恰当的’。下图是肢解的示意图——”
readings_cn.content: “那就说美杜莎的谜语吧，我选择译成‘何物不得见？’还有一道谜语，我听到的译文是‘何物会失去？’要回答此问，我会复述一些历史上著名上的作答——这些作答本身，某种意义上也是，祭品——”

items.name: Gildersleeve's Latin Grammar
items.name_cn: 《吉尔德斯利夫的拉丁语语法》
items.description: Just what you need to refresh your knowledge of Latin.
items.description_cn: 最适于用来复习拉丁语知识。

readings.intro: I recall a certain amount from my school-days, but I need to brush up.
readings.content: The doors of the palace of memory are opened.

readings_cn.intro: 我能回想起不少学生时代的所学，不过我需要复习。
readings_cn.content: 开启记忆宫殿之门。

items.name: The Journal of Alessandro LaCroce
items.name_cn: 《亚历山德罗·拉克罗切的手记》
items.description: Prince Alessandro LaCroce spent years in secret study of the tablets taken from the Fucine Marshes in central Italy. His work will allow you to decipher Fucine texts.
items.description_cn: 亚历山德罗·拉克罗切亲王耗费多年时间暗中钻研从意大利中部富奇诺沼泽获得的碑文。他的研究成果能助你解读富奇诺语文献。

readings.intro: It has something in common with Latin and something else in common with the scratchings of maddened rats.
readings.content: In places it overlaps with languages I know. In other places... well, I can see why they call it 'the tongue of witches'. But I can understand it well enough, now.

readings_cn.intro: 这种语言与拉丁语有着共通之处，也与发狂老鼠的爪痕有着另一种共通之处。
readings_cn.content: 在有些方面，它与我会讲的那些语言一致。但在另一些方面……好吧，我明白他们为什么称这门语言为“女巫的语言”了。不过现在我对它已有足够理解。

items.name: Kühner and Gerth
items.description: Kühner and Gerth's 'Ausführliche Grammatik der griechischen Sprache' - a Greek grammar. An essential weapon for a ferocious struggle with a challenging language.
items.description_cn: 屈内与格特合著的《Ausführliche Grammatik der griechischen Sprache》——“希腊语语法详解”，是与这门颇具挑战性的语言短兵相接时的必备武器。

readings.intro: Of course I have a little Greek already. But I'll need more than a little.
readings.content: A determined and distinctive tongue. But I have the measure of it.

readings_cn.intro: 诚然，我已经学会了希腊语的皮毛。但是我需要的不止是皮毛。
readings_cn.content: 这是一种果断而独特的语言，但我已经掌握了学习方法。

items.name: The Velshorn Inscriptions
items.description: An epic and notably erotic poem describing a rash musician's couplings with, and eventual flaying by, the Red Mother - in both Greek and Phrygian. The intrepid Cal Velshorn found these inscriptions on a temple wall in Halicarnassus, but the same inscription has turned up in a surprising number of other places. [If you speak Greek, you can use this to learn Phrygian.]
items.description_cn: 一部史诗，同时也是十足的艳诗，讲述了一个鲁莽的乐手和“赤红母亲”交合，最终被后者剥皮的故事——以希腊语和弗里吉亚语双语写就。由勇敢的卡尔·维尔朔恩在哈利卡纳苏斯某座神庙墙上发现，然而同样的铭文在它处亦有出现，且数目惊人。[如果你会希腊语，你可以凭借此书学会弗里吉亚语。]

readings.intro: Phrygian, the language of Midas, of Tecmessa, of the priests of Cybele.
readings.content: Something about this language stirs the blood. Perhaps it is fortunate that none now remembers its lost sounds.

readings_cn.intro: 弗里吉亚语，即迈达斯王、忒克墨萨公主、库柏勒的祭司所讲的语言。
readings_cn.content: 这种语言里的某种东西让人热血奔涌。也许现今已无人记得这种失落的语音是一件幸事。

items.name: THE MAGUS VON BRANDT'S AUTHENTIC AND UNIQUE ACCOUNT OF THE TRUE TONGUE OF THE TRUE HOLY LAND OF THE HIGHMOST
items.name_cn: 《术士冯·布兰特的独家信实手记——记至高真圣域之真语言》
items.description: Written excitably and in some haste by a gentleman in the grip of a Transcendentalist enthusiasm, but nevertheless a useful guide to Aramaic.
items.description_cn: （《术士冯·布兰特的独家信实手记——记至高真圣域之真语言》）由某位绅士凭借一种超验主义的热情，亢奋地草草写成，不过无论如何，本书都是一本趁手的亚兰语入门指导。

readings.intro: There is, of course, no single 'Aramaic', but I will learn what I can.
readings.content: I have achieved a basic understanding.

readings_cn.intro: 自然，“亚兰语”不只单一一种，不过我会尽我所能学习。
readings_cn.content: 我已经对其有了基本了解。

items.name: The August Stone
items.description: A tremendous bowl, big as a gong, carved from black basalt, bearing an incantation against demons in Deep Mandaic. The underside bears the same incantation in Aramaic. [If you speak Aramaic, you can use this to learn Deep Mandaic.]
items.description_cn: 硕大的碗状物，尺寸与锣相当，由黑色的玄武岩雕刻而成，碗身铭有对抗恶魔用的渊深曼达安语咒文。碗底则铭有同一咒文的亚兰语版本。[如果你会亚兰语，你可以凭借此书学会渊深曼达安语。]

readings.intro: Mandaic is the language of a Gnostic sect in the remotest part of Persia. Deep Mandaic remains the language of a sect within that sect, but once it was spoken by adepts.
readings.content: This tongue has just enough in common with Aramaic to make my studies possible; but not to make them easy.

readings_cn.intro: 曼达安语是位于波斯最偏远地区的诺斯替派教徒所用的语言。渊深曼达安语只流传于该教派里的一个支派，但讲这种语言的学徒也一度出现过。
readings_cn.content: 这种语言的发音与亚兰语正好有相似之处，足够让我以此入手学习；但这也并非易事。

items.name: Gartside's Sanskrit Reader
items.description: A lucid book which outlines a careful path through the thickets of a vast and complex language.
items.description_cn: 本书思路清晰，为学习这门浩如烟海，错综复杂的语言指出了一条明路。

readings.intro: The name has been translated as 'the refined language'.
readings.content: So many words, such little time. I will keep my reference works close at hand.

readings_cn.intro: 这种语言的名字意为“精炼的语言”。
readings_cn.content: 词汇太多，时间太少。我会在手边常备资料以供参考。

items.name: The Uyrus
items.description: An elaborate ivory sculpture of impossible intricacy. Around and across its surfaces, Sanskrit inscriptions spiral against matching lines of Vak. [If you speak Sanskrit, you can use this to learn Vak, the first language of the world.]
items.description_cn: 一尊复杂到难以置信的象牙雕塑。表面交错盘绕着梵语与对应的伐诃语铭文。[如果你会梵语，你可以凭借此物学习伐诃语——世界最初的语言。]

readings.intro: Do the Hours speak? If they do, this may be the language they use.
readings.content: It has been said that one does not learn Vak, so much as come to know her. Well, now she and I are a little better acquainted.

readings_cn.intro: 司辰会说话吗？如果会，这或许便是祂们使用的语言。
readings_cn.content: 据说伐诃语不是学能学会的，更别提对她了解了。怎么说呢，她与我现在更加熟稔了一点。

items.name: A Collection of Essays
items.description: If the mind is a blade, this is a whetstone. [Study to gain an Erudition: Lesson Learnt, which you may be able to use to increase Reason.]
items.description_cn: 头脑如刀，此书如砥。[研究此卡获得“博闻：学有所成”，可用于增长“理性”。]

readings.intro: Exercise for the intellect.
readings.content: Possibilities -

readings_cn.intro: 锻炼智力。
readings_cn.content: 计算概率——

items.name: A Collection of Poetry
items.description: 'The poet makes himself a seer by an immense, long, deliberate derangement of all the senses...' The opposite of wisdom, thankfully. [Study to gain a Glimmering: Lesson Learnt, which you may be able to use to increase Passion.]
items.description_cn: “诗人有意无限地，长久地搅乱自身的所有感官，获得预见世事的能力……”可喜的是，这与智慧背道而驰。[研究此卡获得“灵感：学有所成”，可用于增长“激情”。]

readings.intro: I'll stoke the fires of my imagination.
readings.content: Glimpses -

readings_cn.intro: 我要让想象力燃得更旺。
readings_cn.content: 迸发灵感——

items.name: Something something DEEP MYSTERIES something
items.name_cn: 惊天秘密！如此这般这般如此
items.description: A dreadful soufflé of half-digested rumour about the 'Secret Worlds' and the irrelevance of contemporary morality, including a catalogue of unlikely, and probably invented, debaucheries. [If I've bought this from a shop, it probably means there is nothing else of interest left in stock.].
items.description_cn: 一篇耸人听闻的花边文章，描述了关于“隐秘世界”的一知半解的传闻和当今道德观如何脱节，内附一份荒唐不经，大概为杜撰而出的纵欲行为概览。[如果我从商店买到了这个，大概说明商店库存里已没有其他有趣的书籍。]

items.name: Meteoric Bullet
items.description: Taenite-iron bullets are occasionally dug from the skeletons of unusual beasts, across Europe, the Middle East and India. Someone has been hunting monsters.
items.description_cn: 偶然从罕见野兽的骸骨中挖出的镍铁子弹，出土地点跨越欧洲，中东及印度。有人曾经猎杀过怪兽。

items.name: Biedde's Blade
items.description: A cut from this blade will not cease bleeding until the wound is healed. One account has it that Biedde was a knife-collecting surgeon-highwayman in eighteenth-century Toulouse. Another claims Biedde is only the bastardisation of an Arabic word for 'mosquito'.
items.description_cn: 这把刀刃割出的伤口会在愈合前不停流血。一说“比德”是十八世纪图卢兹一名喜欢收集刀具的外科医生兼路匪。另一说“比德”只是阿拉伯语“蚊子”的讹传。

items.name: Furious Sliver
items.description: When the Lionsmith turned against the Colonel, he crushed his own sword in his fist. Each tiniest fragment of that weapon still thrills with rage.
items.description_cn: 狮子匠背离上校时，他用自己的拳心碾碎了自己的配剑。此剑的每一小片至今都在因愤怒而颤动。

items.name: Cinnabar Amulet
items.description: Scarlet is the colour of heat. Mercury holds one key to an ultimate dissolution.
items.description_cn: 猩红乃高热之色，而水银则是通往终极融解的钥匙。

items.name: Malleus Imperative
items.description: A tiny ear-bone, blackened by intense heat. Applied correctly, it can crack stone.
items.description_cn: 一块微小的耳骨，已被高热熏黑。使用得当的话，可以击裂石头。

items.name: Carcass Spark
items.description: A remnant of a greater radiance, glowing softly as decay. Just possibly, a mote of the divided Sun.
items.description_cn: 一团更大光线源的残留，随衰变发出柔和的光。它可能是裂分之阳的微粒，只是可能。

items.name: Whispering Amulet
items.description: It knows what I desire; or I imagine that it does.
items.description_cn: 它知道我的欲望；或者在我的想象中它知道。

items.name: Stained Gloves
items.description: What uses have these known? What lessons might they teach my hands?
items.description_cn: 它们以前用作何用呢？能教会我的双手何事呢？

items.name: Hallowed Polos
items.description: The ring-crown of a savage mother, stained with essence, woven with scraps of hair and blessed with flecks of skin.
items.description_cn: 这是一顶属于野人母亲的环冕，上染着萃取液，以零碎毛发编织，并以皮肤残片祝福。

items.name: Chalice Murmurous
items.description: On those nights when we drink from the chalice, we are not certain, afterwards, what we have done. But, we may be assured, it is what always has been done, and if we do not remember, our children will, in their redmost dreams.
items.description_cn: 对于那些我们用此杯饮酒的夜晚，我们后来并不确定我们做了什么。但我们可以确信，我们做了一向会做的事，而且即便我们不记得，我们的孩子也会记得，在他们最猩红的梦中。

items.name: Marruvine Idol
items.description: The Marruvii would make little wooden idols to placate the witch-twins they feared in their lake. The lake is almost dry now, but the idols and the witch-twins yet remain, yet shadowed with the aspect of the Heart.
items.description_cn: 马尔鲁维姆人制作木头小人偶以安抚他们所惧怕的湖中孪生女巫。如今湖水基本干涸，但湖底的人偶和孪生女巫仍存，虽然被心之性相所荫蔽。

items.name: Wakeful Tympanum
items.description: In the grove where they flayed the thunder, they rattled their instruments to rouse the frenzy. The power still clings, like scent.
items.description_cn: 在他们将雷鸣剥皮的小林子里，他们狂敲手上的器具来激起暴怒之情。那股力量萦绕不去，如同气味。

items.name: Kingskin Bodhrán
items.description: In the deep forests, the monarch gave up the last thing they had to give, and so the tool was shaped to keep their land forever safe. Then, of course, an empire stole it, as empires do.
items.description_cn: 密林中，那位君主交出了他不得不交出的最后一样东西，以之造出此永庇疆土之器。后来，可想而知，一个帝国盗走了这面鼓，用帝国一贯的做法。

items.name: Icon of St Agnes
items.description: St Agnes of Bohemia was renowned for her pious dedication to the mortification of the flesh. This icon makes for grisly viewing.
items.description_cn: 波希米亚的圣亚割妮因虔诚地追求苦修肉身而闻名。该徽记形状可怖。

items.name: Consecrated Lintel
items.description: This is the skull of a door through which power has passed.
items.description_cn: 这是一扇神灵曾穿过的门的颅骨。

items.name: Frangiclave
items.description: There are keys that open doors; then there are keys that destroy them.
items.description_cn: 有用来开门的钥匙，也有用来毁门的钥匙。

items.name: Noonstone
items.description: Noon, the saying goes, is not what it was; but this polished stone still retains a sunset glow.
items.description_cn: “午的含义，在现代的语言中，已经和古语有所不同。但是，这块石头仍透着夕阳般的光彩。

items.name: Wildering Mirror
items.description: A multiplicity of vistas! A bewilderment of views! Gaze upon me, and rejoice in the dissolution of your senses!
items.description_cn: 多重景观！迷乱视觉！盯着我，以你五感的融解取乐吧！

items.name: Watchman's Glass
items.description: This is the mirror into which one does not look twice.
items.description_cn: 这是一面不可注视第二回的镜子。

items.name: Wingèd Doll
items.description: In an attic above a skeleton house there was a window. Beside the window there was a box. In the box there was a bandage. In the bandage was a twist of clotted hair. In the hair was wound a doll, because the window had never been opened.
items.description_cn: 白骨屋上的阁楼有扇窗子。窗子旁边有个盒子。盒子里面有卷绷带。绷带里面有团乱发。乱发里面缠着只人偶，因为窗户从未打开过。

items.name: Dappled Mask
items.description: In the forest where the moon couldn't go, the boughs of the trees were woven together like bandages or lovers. The moon might change herself to an ant or to a bird or to her sister, but the forest would not yield to her penetrations, no matter her caresses. One day we came with our scissors, and we severed the branches until the moon and the blood dappled the rotting leaves on the forest floor.
items.description_cn: 在月光照不进的森林之中，树枝像绑带或恋人一样缠在一起。月亮将自己变成一只蚂蚁，一只小鸟或自己的姐妹，但不管她如何爱抚森林，森林仍然抗拒她进入。有一天我们携剪子前来，斩断树枝，直到月光和鲜血斑驳地撒树底的腐叶上。

items.name: Alakapurine Shears
items.description: In the North there is a city of great wealth where dwelt a protector of the world. One day he fell silent. These shears were used to take from him first his hair and then his fingers and then what remained.
items.description_cn: 北方有一座富庶的城市，里面曾住着一名世界的守护者。他有一天陷入了永恒的沉寂。这把剪刀被用来先剪他的头发，再剪他的手指，然后剪剩下的一切。

items.name: Paradoxical Curio
items.description: Sometimes, it is hard to be sure if an arrow slew the Empress Herodias, or the Empress Eudokia. Sometimes, it is possible that an ormolu clock was stolen in the sack of Vienna even as it rested safe in the vaults of Rome.
items.description_cn: 有时，很难确定一只箭究竟是杀了希罗底皇后还是欧多克西亚皇后。有时，一只镀金钟有可能既在维也纳遭洗劫时被盗，也在罗马的藏宝地里安放着。

items.name: Atlas of Dreams
items.description: The shape of the world changes in each past, but the shape of the Mansus is reflected in all of them. One cannot map the Mansus, but one can make an attempt to map its reflections.
items.description_cn: 世界的形状在每个过去中都有所变化，但里面都倒映出了漫宿的形状。人虽不能为漫宿绘制地图，却可以尝试绘制它的倒影。

items.name: Bone Flute
items.description: Its sound will cease.
items.description_cn: 此物的声响将会停歇。

items.name: Elagabaline Manacle
items.description: It does not relinquish its grip.
items.description_cn: 此物不会放松钳制。

items.name: Division Bell
items.description: First, its voice, and after, nothing.
items.description_cn: 先由此铃发声，而后一无所响。

items.name: Cracked Noonstone
items.description: Noon, the saying goes, is not what it was; but this stone still retains an embery glow. It has been cracked. A Forge-aspected follower could restore it, with sufficient resources - or I could use up what power remains in it.
items.description_cn: “午的含义，在现代的语言中，已经和古语有所不同。但是，这块石头仍透着夕阳般的光彩。它已经被裂开了。如果有相应的材料，铸相的追随者应该可以将其复原——又或者，我可以用光里面残余的法力。

items.name: Cracked Wildering Mirror
items.description: A deep crack runs across the shimmering metal. A Forge-aspected follower could repair it, with sufficient resources - or I could use up what power remains in it.
items.description_cn: 一道深深的裂痕划过这块亮灿灿的金属。如果有相应的材料，铸相追随者可以将其修复——又或者，我可以用光里面残余的法力。

items.name: Cracked Watchman's Glass
items.description: A Forge-aspected follower could repair it, but the cost would be high - or I could use up what power remains in it.
items.description_cn: 铸相的追随者可以将其修复，但代价高昂——又或者，我可以用光里面残余的法力。

items.name: 'Colonel and Lionsmith'
items.description: Since Issus have they striven so.
items.description_cn: 自伊苏斯时代他们便起纷争。

items.name: 'The Forge of Days'
items.description: If the Forge could regret, it would regret the Intercalate, but in all its other work, it knows joy.
items.description_cn: 如果铸炉可以悔恨，它会为置闰而悔恨，但对它其余的作为，它感到快乐。

items.name: 'The Red Grail'
items.description: She did not split the Sun, but here we might imagine how she must have desired it.
items.description_cn: 她并没有分裂太阳，但我们可以想象她一定曾经渴望过。

items.name: 'The Sister-and-Witch'
items.description: She has been a pair of funeral birds, but here she is as she would wish to drown.
items.description_cn: 她一直是一对成双的送葬鸟，而画中的她就如她本希望的一样溺亡。

items.name: 'The Mother of Ants'
items.description: Even in the days of Elam, she had begun to appear thus.
items.description_cn: 打在埃兰时，她就已现出这样的外貌。

items.name: 'The Door in the Eye'
items.description: He came from the Glory. We cannot help but see.
items.description_cn: 他来自辉光。我们情不自禁要看它。

items.name: 'The Moth'
items.description: In the forests of the first continent, our ancestors cursed themselves with their own god.
items.description_cn: 在第一大陆的森林中，我们的祖先诅咒自己的神连带诅咒自己。

items.name: 'Teresa and Christopher'
items.description: Love, like the Mansus, defies boundaries.
items.description_cn: 漫宿无墙，爱亦无疆。

items.name: 'The Wolf-Divided'
items.description: CAPUT GERAT LUPINUM. The Sun was divided, and this is its wound.
items.description_cn: CAPUT GERAT LUPINUM。太阳曾被分裂，此即其伤口。

items.name: A Pale Canvas
items.description: I must go very carefully. The memories that I need to convey will take flight from the canvas if I depict them too strongly. I will find those memories in the flesh of the dead... and perhaps even, if I must, in my own dying flesh.
items.description_cn: 我运笔必须非常小心。要是用力过重，我要表达的回忆会从画布上飞走。我会在亡者的肉体中寻见这些回忆，甚至也许，在我自己将死的肉体中。

items.name: The Palest Painting
items.description: 'Six were lost, thirty remain.' The canvas is not white. Look closely, and see the hinted shapes of the Hours long lost, walking the winding path to the door into Nowhere. Look too closely, and find yourself lost to weeping.
items.description_cn: “六者已失，卅者留存。”画布不是白色的。凑近看，你将隐约看到早已失落的司辰的形影，沿曲折的路途走进通往虚界之门。凑得太近，你将湎于落泪而不能自拔。

items.name: Martensite Paste
items.description: The sacred chrysm of the sword. Also an attractive silver-green.
items.description_cn: 涂剑用的圣油。且有着迷人的银绿色。

items.name: Labhitic Grains
items.description: Labhites are the youngest of the Lionsmith's servants. When rendered to powder, they retain their potency but not their beauty.
items.description_cn: 狻猊是狮子匠最年轻的仆从。磨成粉后，它效力依旧，却不复美丽。

items.name: Skaptodon Fang
items.description: It is rare for the Lionsmith to make skaptodons, now; but they are difficult to kill, and they live a very long time.
items.description_cn: 狮子匠如今甚少制造剑齿兽了；但是它们很难杀死，而且寿命极长。

items.name: Bitterblack Salts
items.description: No ordinary chemist could produce these dark-gleaming crystals - not without the touch of the Forge.
items.description_cn: 没有哪个普通的化学家能制造出这种黑亮的晶体——若离了铸炉的触碰。

items.name: Xanthotic Essence
items.description: In certain operations of the Forge, sunlight is said to overcome moonlight, as we pass from the Meniscate to the Madrugad. This essence was mercury, once, but now it's the rich gold of a summer afternoon. Pretty.
items.description_cn: 在铸炉的某些行动中，据说日光会驱散月光，如同我们从弧月的钟点过渡到昕旦的钟点。这种精华曾是水银，不过它现在为夏日午后的浓金色。很漂亮。

items.name: Iotic Essence
items.description: In the later operations of the Forge, the Madrugad yields to the true Forge of Days, and the essence begins to redden. Some day, perhaps, it will not, but for now we have this.
items.description_cn: 在铸炉的后期运转中，昕旦让位于真正的白日铸炉，这种精华也开始变红。也许有一天，变红会停止，不过现下我们还有的可用。

items.name: Vital Pigment
items.description: It is not usual for a red this red to survive the death of the body.
items.description_cn: 躯体死后还保留如此红的红色，并不寻常。

items.name: Amaranthine Nectar
items.description: One of the Flowermaker's many gifts. In a brighter age, it might have bestowed immortality. In this blighted History, it is still an unparalleled sweetness.
items.description_cn: 制花人的繁多赠礼之一。在更加光明的年代，它或许被赐予了永生。即使在这重枯萎的历史中，它依旧拥有无法比拟的甜腻。

items.name: Writhing Caul
items.description: Lay your hand on these tattered folds and feel their warmth; leave your hand upon it, and it will explore the possibilities of embrace.
items.description_cn: 把你的手置于它残破的褶皱上，感受它的温暖；手不收回，则它将探索拥抱的可能性。

items.name: Rose-Pearl Dust
items.description: Pearls are sacred to the Witch-and-Sister, especially those of this colour. They have been used in protective rites, among others.
items.description_cn: 珍珠对双生巫女而言是神圣的，特别是这种颜色的。它们尤其被用在防护性的仪式中。

items.name: Witch-Kissed Oil
items.description: The formula remains unchanged since the days Hecate was worshipped at the crossways.
items.description_cn: 从女神赫卡忒在十字路受人敬拜始，这个配方从未改变过。

items.name: True Blood of St Januarius
items.description: The Thunderskin protected the one they called Januarius, against perils from every past. To this day his blood keeps dancing.
items.description_cn: 轰雷之皮在每一个过去中保护了一个人称“雅纳略”的人免遭危难。时至如今，他的血液仍在持续舞动。

items.name: The Byzantine Tinct
items.description: The profound purple worn only in Histories where Tyrian dye was not rich enough for emperors. It is difficult to bar entry to one wearing this colour.
items.description_cn: 这种深奥的紫色只在“推罗紫”染料不够浓重的历史中才用于穿着。穿这种颜色的人到哪里都出入无禁。

items.name: Sthenic Venom
items.description: From time to time, the Mother of Ants has also been called the Daughter of Venoms. This substance opens the body in uncountable places.
items.description_cn: 蚁母时而也被称为“毒液的女儿”。这种物质在不计其数的地方洞开着人体。

items.name: Azoth
items.description: Store this only in containers of a pure element, and never permit it to grow warm. Perhaps it isn't the final solvent that the alchemists sought. But it will do, for our purposes.
items.description_cn: 此物只能储存在纯由一种元素制成的容器，且绝对不能容许它加温。它或许不是炼金术士追寻的终极溶剂。但它能胜任我们的目的。

items.name: Refulgin
items.description: A white so pure that it remains visible even in utter darkness.
items.description_cn: 至纯的白色，在全然的黑暗中依然可见。

items.name: Glassfinger Toxin
items.description: 'What is within, without; what is without, within.' A poison sacred to the votaries of the Meniscate.
items.description_cn: “内外相易，表里互替。”一种对弧月信徒来说地位神圣的毒素。

items.name: Ichor Vitreous
items.description: A pale and watchful fluid that can be gathered, sometimes, when the Door-in-the-Eye is opened.
items.description_cn: 有的时候，瞳中扉打开时，可以收集到一种浅色的，警觉的液体。

items.name: Piebald Pigment
items.description: From the crushed wings of rare lepidopterans. 'Painting black, or painting white, this is the stuff that'll see you right.'
items.description_cn: 取自碾碎的稀有鳞翅目昆虫的翅膀。“想画黑，想画白，这种颜料都能来。”

items.name: Leathy
items.description: A dark and syrupy liquor favoured in unnamed forest villages. 'The tongue and the eye, and now we begin! Forget your name, forget your skin.'
items.description_cn: 一种粘稠的黑色液体，受到森林中无名村落的喜爱。“舌头与眼睛，现在我们开始！忘记你的名字，忘记你的表皮。”

items.name: Holiest Hemolymph
items.description: Faint traces of an enigmatic substance spilt in the commission of an ancient crime, tightly sealed in a glass ampoule. 'Who will remember the barber's son?'
items.description_cn: 某桩古老罪案现场洒落的神秘物质的淡淡印痕，紧封在一个安瓿瓶中。“谁会记得理发师的儿子？”

items.name: Greydawn Oil
items.description: The precise colour of the hours when one cannot sleep.
items.description_cn: 正是人于之无法入眠的时辰的颜色。

items.name: Wolf-Snow
items.description: Far too cold ever to melt in anything but the hottest noonday sun. It will, very gradually, consume human flesh.
items.description_cn: 此物冷到任何事物都无法将之融化，除了最炎热的正午阳光。它会一点一点，极缓地蚕食人类的血肉。

items.name: Watch-Worms
items.description: A tiny pot of stunted, desiccated larval remnants from the First Worm War, rank with the power that inhabits dead Hours.
items.description_cn: 第一次蠕虫大战遗留下的一小罐发育不良的，干瘪的幼虫，与占据已逝众司辰之位的神灵同级。

items.name: A Knife's Secret
items.description: When our ancestors forged swords, taught the arts of martial movement, spoke curses on the eve of battle - all these things shared certain patterns. [Use this in a Rite with a corpse and Winter power, and the corpse will rise.]
items.description_cn: 我们的祖先铸造刀剑、教授武艺、在战争前夕咒骂——这些行为都遵循相同的规律。[在仪式中与尸体及冬之力一同运用，可使尸体复生。]

items.name: Chiliarch's Lesson
items.description: This is the bone-deep story the thousandman learnt in antiquity, of blood and its exits. To speak it aloud is to hear the sword hiss. [Use this in a Rite with a corpse and Winter power, and the corpse will rise.]
items.description_cn: 千夫长在悠久的过去中学到了有关于鲜血和伤口的刻骨故事。刀剑嘶鸣声，正大声诉说着这个故事。[在仪式中与尸体及冬之力一同运用，可使尸体复生。]

items.name: An Operation of the Labhite
items.description: A series of mystic exercises that requires both dedication and terror. [Use this in a Rite with a corpse and Winter power, and the corpse will rise.]
items.description_cn: 一系列需要为之献身、为之惊骇的神秘活动。[在仪式中与尸体及冬之力一同运用，可使尸体复生。]

items.name: The Colonel's Names
items.description: The Colonel has been many things in many ages. He is blind; he is deaf; he cannot be wounded; he cannot be denied. His Names are cunning as only the very old can be.
items.description_cn: 上校在不同的时代有着不同的形象。他目盲；他耳聋；他不受创伤；他不容违抗。他的具名者皆如极年迈之人一般狡诈。

items.name: The Lionsmith's Names
items.description: The Lionsmith is young by the standards of the Hours, but old by the standards of war. His Names are recent recruits, and their recitation has a savage power.
items.description_cn: 狮子匠，按司辰的标准来看尚显青涩，而按战争的标准来看相当老成。他的具名者皆是刚被招募的新成员，其吟诵有一种野蛮的力量。

items.name: The Alignments of Murder
items.description: These are the arts that ensure an ending.
items.description_cn: 此为确保终结的技艺。

items.name: The Mysteries of Force
items.description: The Colonel and the Lionsmith are gods-who-were-flesh, but the Wolf-Divided is a god-who-was-blood. Cunning, Strength and Agony are the three roots of victory, and here is their secret doctrine...
items.description_cn: 上校和狮子匠是肉源之神，但是裂分之狼是血源之神。狡诈、力气与痛苦乃胜利的三大根基，下文即其秘密教义……

items.name: A Smith's Secret
items.description: In five continents, smiths have whispered the same words to the iron. Murderers have been known to whisper these words, too. And adepts, of course. These words are spoken in ritual to inspire an unmerciful Change.
items.description_cn: 在五块大陆上，铁匠对钢铁低语相同的字句。众所周知，杀人犯也会低语这些字句。而学徒自然也是如此。在仪式中念出这些字句可激发出无情的改变。

items.name: An Ardent Orison
items.description: When we watch a fire, what are we watching for? When we find it, these are the words it will speak: a word that sanctifies the change that comes when the seared skin peels.
items.description_cn: 当我们注视火焰时，我们所视何物？我们找到此物时，它会说出：一个赋予转变神性的词汇，此改变随烧焦的皮肤剥落而出现。

items.name: A Shaping Chant
items.description: The proper words must be employed when the Change comes. [Use this in a Rite with a Knock influence and a Bone Flute - or other resources of equal power - to summon a Caligine.]
items.description_cn: 当改变来临之际，必须运用恰当的知识。[将其与启之影响以及骨笛——或其他拥有同等法力的材料——一同运用于仪式中，可召唤汽灵。]

items.name: Callidate Invocation
items.description: The Names of the Forge have all spoken these words. [Use this in a Rite with a Knock influence and a Bone Flute - or other resources of equal power - to summon a Caligine.]
items.description_cn: 铸之具名者都念诵过这些话语。[将其与启之影响以及骨笛——或其他拥有同等法力的材料——一同运用于仪式中，可召唤汽灵。]

items.name: Formula Fissive
items.description: Break a thing, and you have fragments. Break those fragments, and you have dust. Break the dust, and then break what remains. Here is fire. [Use this in a Rite with a Consecrated Lintel and a little Refulgin - or other resources of equal power - to summon King Crucible.]
items.description_cn: 破坏一样东西，你就能得到片段。破坏那些片段，你就能得到尘埃。破坏尘埃，然后再破坏它的残余。就这样，你得到了火。[将其与祝圣门楣以及少量耀素——或其他拥有同等法力的材料——一同运用于仪式中，可召唤坩埚王。]

items.name: Furnace Paean
items.description: This is the hymn the heat sings to the iron. If we imitate it faithfully enough we will parch our lips and crisp our tongue, but O, the rewards. [Use this in a Rite with a Consecrated Lintel and a little Refulgin - or other resources of equal power - to summon King Crucible.]
items.description_cn: 这是热力向钢铁吟唱的赞歌。如果我们如实模仿，会使嘴唇干裂，舌头脱水。但是，哦！回报多么丰厚。[将其与祝圣门楣以及少量耀素——或其他拥有同等法力的材料——一同运用于仪式中，可召唤坩埚王。]

items.name: Mysteries of Making
items.description: The Forge of Days, the Meniscate and the Madrugad are gods-from-Light. Mercury, silver and gold are the seeds of the Work, and here is their secret doctrine... [Use this in a Rite with a Consecrated Lintel and a little Refulgin - or other resources of equal power - to summon King Crucible.]
items.description_cn: 白日铸炉、弧月和昕旦是光源之神。汞、银和金乃功业的种穰，下文即其秘密教义……[将其与祝圣门楣以及少量耀素——或其他拥有同等法力的材料——一同运用于仪式中，可召唤坩埚王。]

items.name: A Red Secret
items.description: Some words are spelt correctly only when the proper ink is used.
items.description_cn: 只有使用了适当的墨水，一些字词才能拼写正确。

items.name: A Megalesian Incantation
items.description: The Great Mother remembers.
items.description_cn: 伟大母亲永记不忘。

items.name: A Delightful Sacrament
items.description: So pleasant upon the ear. One could listen over and over. These are the words that make sacrifice sweet. [Use this with Byzantine Tinct and a Moth influence - or other resources of equal power - to summon a Raw Prophet.]
items.description_cn: 多么悦耳啊。让人想要一遍又一遍地聆听。正是这些话语使献祭变得甘甜。[将其与“拜占庭染剂”和蛾之影响——或其他拥有同等法力的材料——一同运用于仪式中，可召唤原生先知。]

items.name: Thiatic Invocation
items.description: Raucous shrieks attend the passage of the Names of the Grail. We reproduce them as best we can, for the pulsing power they lend. [Use this with Byzantine Tinct and a Moth influence - or other resources of equal power - to summon a Raw Prophet.]
items.description_cn: 杯之具名者的典仪进程有刺耳尖叫声的参与。我们要尽可能地重现这些声音，以求得其所提供的搏动之力。[将其与“拜占庭染剂”和蛾之影响——或其他拥有同等法力的材料——一同运用于仪式中，可召唤原生先知。]

items.name: Formulae Voluptuous
items.description: There exist some pleasures intense enough to corrupt the laws of the physical world. [This formula can be used in a Rite with Bitterblack Salts and a Subtle Rupture - or similar sources of power - to summon Ezeem itself.]
items.description_cn: 有些快感如此强烈，足以侵蚀现实世界的法则。[将该法术与“苦黑盐”和“轻微的豁口”——或类似的法力源——一同运用于仪式中，可召唤伊泽姆本人。]

items.name: Anthic Elaboration
items.description: The Flowermaker cannot touch you; he cannot find you; he always has what you desire. Even an elaboration of the properties of his works can draw the attention of Hours. [This formula can be used in a Rite with Bitterblack Salts and a Subtle Rupture - or similar sources of power - to summon Ezeem itself.]
items.description_cn: 制花人无法碰触你；他无法找到你；他永远拥有你欲求的东西。哪怕是细述他作品之精巧的言论也能引起众司辰注意。[将该法术与“苦黑盐”和“轻微的豁口”——或类似的法力源——一同运用于仪式中，可召唤伊泽姆本人。]

items.name: Devouring Mysteries
items.description: The Grail was the first god-who-was-blood. The Flowermaker came from Light. The Beach-Crow was flesh. Hunger and Greed and Yearning are the matrix of appetite, and here is their secret doctrine...  [Use this formula in Rite with Bitterblack Salts and a Subtle Rupture - or similar sources of power - to summon Ezeem itself.]
items.description_cn: 圣杯是第一位血源之神。制花人来自于光。拾滩鸦曾是肉身。“饥饿”、“贪婪”和“渴求”乃食欲的苗床，下文即其秘密教义……[将该法术与“苦黑盐”和“轻微的豁口”——或类似的法力源——一同运用于仪式中，可召唤伊泽姆本人。]

items.name: A Thunderous Secret
items.description: There are common sentiments in every thunderclap. Let us acknowledge them.
items.description_cn: 每一声雷霆都蕴含着共通的情绪。让我们向它们致意吧。

items.name: Words that Walk
items.description: The syllables of this formula are compelling. I find myself snapping my fingers to its rhythm. It desires not to cease.
items.description_cn: 这个法术的音节扣人心弦。我发现自己正跟随节拍打着响指。它与我都不想停歇。

items.name: A Waking Chant
items.description: Who could hear this and remain unmoved? The sleeping? The dead? The earth and the sky? [Use this in a Rite with Byzantine Tinct and a Meteoric Bullet - or other resources of equal power - to summon a Percussigant.]
items.description_cn: 谁听后能依然无动于衷？沉睡之人？离世之人？大地与天空？[将其与“拜占庭染剂”和“陨铁子弹”——或其他拥有同等法力的材料——一同运用于仪式中，可召唤擂击者。]

items.name: Geminate Invocation
items.description: The Sister-and-Witch has always been invoked for protection, at crossroads and at moonrise and where the land shelters the sea. [Use this in a Rite with Byzantine Tinct and a Meteoric Bullet - or other resources of equal power - to summon a Percussigant.]
items.description_cn: 人们总是祈求双生女巫的护佑，于十字路口，于月初时分，于陆地庇护大海之处。[将其与“拜占庭染剂”和“陨铁子弹”——或其他拥有同等法力的材料——一同运用于仪式中，可召唤擂击者。]

items.name: Formulae Vigilant
items.description: One who watches does not sleep, one who sleeps watches not. One who watches does not sleep, one who sleeps watches not. [Use this in a Rite with Byzantine Tinct and a Meteoric Bullet - or other resources of equal power - to summon a Percussigant.]
items.description_cn: 守夜者不入眠，入眠者不守夜。守夜者不入眠，入眠者不守夜。[将其与“拜占庭染剂”和“陨铁子弹”——或其他拥有同等法力的材料——一同运用于仪式中，可召唤擂击者。]

items.name: Velvet Charm
items.description: The Velvet always answers 'No', but we can shelter in that 'No' like beasts in the crook of a tree. [Use this in a Rite with Byzantine Tinct and a Meteoric Bullet - or other resources of equal power - to summon a Percussigant.]
items.description_cn: 丝毧总以否定作答，然而我们能在那声否定中得到荫蔽，就像野兽藏于树杈间。[将其与“拜占庭染剂”和“陨铁子弹”——或其他拥有同等法力的材料——一同运用于仪式中，可召唤擂击者。]

items.name: Unceasing Mysteries
items.description: The Grail ripped the Thunderskin from flesh. The Sister-and-Witch was born from two wombs. The Velvet woke when the Wood-roots tasted blood. The Heart is Blood's Drum, and here is its secret doctrine... [Use this in a Rite with Byzantine Tinct and a Meteoric Bullet - or other resources of equal power - to summon a Percussigant.]
items.description_cn: 圣杯将轰雷之皮从肉体撕下。双生女巫生于两个子宫。丝毧觉醒于在林地根部尝到血的味道时。心脏乃鲜血之鼓，下文即其秘密教义……[将其与“拜占庭染剂”和“陨铁子弹”——或其他拥有同等法力的材料——一同运用于仪式中，可召唤擂击者。]

items.name: A Locksmith's Secret
items.description: Sooner or later, every locksmith has the Dream. Now we recite its seven phases... [Nearly every summoning Rite requires Knock influence. This lore will provide it.]
items.description_cn: 每个锁匠迟早会做梦。现在我们来背诵它的七个阶段吧……[几乎所有召唤仪式都需要启之影响，此密传可提供之。]

items.name: An Iguvine Rite
items.description: Every door in the Mansus requires its sacrifice before it will open. The Iguvine Rites prescribe the manner of the sacrifice. [Nearly every summoning Rite requires Knock influence. This lore will provide it.]
items.description_cn: 漫宿的每一道门在开启前都需要献祭。伊库维姆诸仪式则规定了献祭的方式。[几乎所有召唤仪式都需要启之影响，此密传可提供之。]

items.name: A Consent of Wounds
items.description: To open certain Ways, one must first open oneself. This practice outlines that opening, in the name of the Mother of Ants. [Nearly every summoning Rite requires Knock influence. This lore will provide it.]
items.description_cn: 要开启某些道路，人必须先开启自己。此种修炼将以蚁母之名的开启之法概括其中。[几乎所有召唤仪式都需要启之影响，此密传可提供之。]

items.name: Meniscate Invocation
items.description: When the moon's face was wounded, these words appeared. [Nearly every summoning Rite requires Knock influence. This lore will provide it.]
items.description_cn: 当月亮的脸上添了伤口，这些字句便出现了。[几乎所有召唤仪式都需要启之影响，此密传可提供之。]

items.name: Formulae Ophidian
items.description: Serpents are the visitors which may not be denied. [Nearly every summoning Rite requires Knock influence. This lore will provide it.]
items.description_cn: 蛇是不容拒绝的访客。[几乎所有召唤仪式都需要启之影响，此密传可提供之。]

items.name: Liminal Evocation
items.description: One god-who-was-stone remains, and she watches all thresholds. [Nearly every summoning Rite requires Knock influence. This lore will provide it.]
items.description_cn: 仍有一位石源之神留存，她看守着所有的门关。[几乎所有召唤仪式都需要启之影响，此密传可提供之。]

items.name: Mysteries of Opening
items.description: The Mother of Ants is the child of two rivers. The Horned-Axe is the last god-from-Stone. The Meniscate was born in the Moon from Light. The Wound and the Threshold and the Revelation are all the Gate's aspects, and here is their secret doctrine... [Nearly every summoning Rite requires Knock influence. This lore will provide it.]
items.description_cn: 蚁母是两河的孩子。双角斧是最后的石源之神。弧月源于光，生于月亮。伤口、门槛和揭示皆乃门的面相，下文即其秘密教义……[几乎所有召唤仪式都需要启之影响，此密传可提供之。]

items.name: A Watchman's Secret
items.description: It has been expressed like this: 'Each Hour has its colour, but colour exists only where there is light.'
items.description_cn: 其表述如下：“司辰各有其颜色，但颜色只存在于有光的地方。”

items.name: A Mansus-Glimpse
items.description: A snatch of poetry; a single memory of a certain house that all of us visit at least twice in our lives. For one's first visit to the Mansus, this lore is almost essential.
items.description_cn: 诗章的只言片语；关于我们所有人在一生中都至少要造访两次的某座房屋的一次回忆。对于第一次来到漫宿的人来说，此密传几乎是必不可少的。

items.name: An Unmerciful Mantra
items.description: 'Mercy', saith the Watchman, 'is found only in shadow.'
items.description_cn: “仁慈，”守夜人道，“仅能在影中觅得。”

items.name: Phanaean Invocation
items.description: The Door-in-the-Eye navigates; he is not merciful; but first and always, he illuminates. [Use this in a Rite with a Knock tool and a Thrilling Air - or other resources of equal power - to summon a Hint from behind mirrors.]
items.description_cn: 瞳中扉指引前路；他并不仁慈；然而从始至今，他一直在照明驱暗。[将其与启之工具以及“激振的气氛”——或其他拥有同等法力的材料——一同运用于仪式中，可从镜子后召唤迹形。]

items.name: Formulae Concursate
items.description: The Concursum waits at the Lantern of the Mansus. It has been called the Chamber of Ways and also the Chamber of Endings. Its intricacies are probably beyond human comprehension, but these formulae are a first approximation. [Use this in a Rite with a Knock tool and a Thrilling Air - or other resources of equal power - to summon a Hint from behind mirrors.]
items.description_cn: 聚点于漫宿之灯处守候。它又被称作道路之室，还有结尾之室。其错综复杂或许超出了人类的理解范围，但这些法术可以对其进行基本的近似。[将其与启之工具以及“激振的气氛”——或其他拥有同等法力的材料——一同运用于仪式中，可从镜子背后召唤迹形。]

items.name: Mantra of Ascent
items.description: The Ascent of Knives is the bloodiest of the Watchman's tests. Those who pass it and are dead enter the service of the Sun-in-Rags. Those living who pass it are a little closer to the Glory. [Use this in a Rite with a Knock tool and a Thrilling Air - or other resources of equal power - to summon a Hint from behind mirrors.]
items.description_cn: 刀刃阶梯是守夜人最血腥的考验。行过此梯且已死去之人都受到了残阳的接待。而活着的行过此梯之人都距辉光近了一点点。[将其与启之工具以及“激振的气氛”——或其他拥有同等法力的材料——一同运用于仪式中，可从镜子后召唤迹形。]

items.name: Illuminate Mysteries
items.description: The Meniscate, the Madrugad, the Flowermaker and the Forge of Days are the gods-from-Light. There is a fifth, but now we know it is not the Watchman. Yet the Watchman shares a secret doctrine with those five, and here is that doctrine... [Use this in a Rite with a Subtle Rupture and a Paradoxical Curio, and someone will come. Speak it to a Hunter, and it might drive them insane on the spot.]
items.description_cn: 弧月、昕旦、制花人和白日铸炉是光源之神。尚有第五位，但现在我们知道那不是守夜人。不过守夜人仍与前五者共用一条秘密教义，下文即此秘密教义……[将其与“轻微的豁口”和“矛盾的古董”一同运用于仪式中，而后某位将来临。将其告知猎人，则会使他当场发疯。]

items.name: A Barber's Warning
items.description: A power of the Wood enjoys the separation of the lock from the scalp. For attention, burn it. For opportunity, bury it. [Speak this over a corpse in a Rite, with a Winter influence present, and the corpse will rise.]
items.description_cn: 一位林地之神乐于将缕缕发丝从头皮上分离。以求关注，则将之焚烧。以求机遇，则将之埋葬。[在仪式中将其对一具尸体念诵，加上冬之影响，可使尸体复生。]

items.name: A Wood-Whisper
items.description: Lie awake, and listen. The wind speaks in the branches. The house cries out in its sleep. These are the roads that chaos rides. [Speak this over a corpse in a Rite, with a Winter influence present, and the corpse will rise.]
items.description_cn: 夜不能寐，侧耳聆听。微风穿梭于枝桠间，窃窃私语。房屋沉溺于自己的梦中，大声呼号。这皆是混沌所经之路。[在仪式中将其对一具尸体念诵，加上冬之影响，可使尸体复生。]

items.name: An Ecdysiast's Parable
items.description: The Ecdysiast's Riddle is 'What may be lost?' Each Ecdysiast's Parable is an attempt to answer the Riddle.
items.description_cn: 蜕衣舞者的谜语是：“何物会失去？”每个蜕衣舞者的寓言都是回答谜语的一次尝试。

items.name: Moldywarp Admonitions
items.description: Moldywarp keeps her crowns in the moss and her feet in the dirt and the trees locked jaw-tight. Moldywarp has these warnings for you.
items.description_cn: 鼹鼠的头顶覆满青苔，双脚深陷泥土，且使树木被紧锁住。此文是鼹鼠给你的警告。

items.name: Centipede Testament
items.description: The Centipede came up out of the sands and went in under the roots. She found a new home but now she can't go home. She creeps in everywhere else: keyholes and histories and the channels of birth and sight and hearing. Here's what she has to say.
items.description_cn: 蜈蚣自沙中来，往根下去。她找到了一个新家，但现在永远也回不去了。她在除此之外的所有地方爬过：锁眼，诸历史，还有生育的、视觉的、听觉的通道。此文是她要说的话。

items.name: Thigh-born Thorax-Sweet
items.description: Vine-crowned moth-king hatched in the thigh of the thunder-king who's dead. Drink up his belly-lymph. These are the sights you'll see.
items.description_cn: 藤冠的飞蛾王在死去的轰雷王的大腿处孵化。饮尽他腹部的淋巴液。上述为你将看到的景象。

items.name: Mare-in-the-Yew
items.description: The real Hours don't meet the gods-from-Nowhere, but the Ring-Yew meets the Mare-in-the-Tree in where the Wood grows lush. Their couplings are forbidden, and forbidden things have power, and this is the story of their couplings.
items.description_cn: 真正的司辰不会面见虚源之神，环杉却在林地茂盛处与树中牝马会面。她们的交合是被禁止的，而被禁止的事物拥有力量。此即他们交合的故事。

items.name: An Occult Scrap
items.description: Secret histories are layered beneath the one we know, like the notes in rare wine. This is a detail from one of those histories. [Exploring with this scrap of knowledge may uncover secret locations in the Capital.]
items.description_cn: 隐秘的历史被掩盖于我们所知的历史之下，就像珍贵红酒的气味。这便是其中一重历史中的一个细节。[用此知识残篇探索，或可发现都城的秘密地点。]

items.name: A Furtive Truth
items.description: A detail smuggled in from an adjacent narrative. Don't speak this where you may be overheard. [Exploring with this scrap of knowledge may uncover secret locations in the Shires.]
items.description_cn: 从毗邻的故事中悄然透露出的一个细节。不要在可能被窃听的地方谈论这个。[用此知识残篇探索，或可发现各郡的秘密地点。]

items.name: A Forgotten Chronicle
items.description: A story of a city without a gate, of a queen who was not born, of a war which was not fought. [Exploring with this scrap of knowledge may uncover secret locations on the Continent.]
items.description_cn: 一段故事，有关于一座没有大门的城市，一位非曾出生的女王，一场非曾打起的战争。[用此知识残篇探索，或可发现大陆上的秘密地点。]

items.name: Forbidden Epic
items.description: The attention of the Hours is drawn to the bloodiest wars. Afterwards, the Histories are braided like hair. [Exploring with this scrap of knowledge may uncover secret locations in the Land Beyond the Forest, across the Continent.]
items.description_cn: 众司辰被最为血腥的战争吸引了注意。而后，重重历史被编结如发辫。[用此知识残篇探索，或可发现在大陆另一端，森林尽头之地中的秘密地点。]

items.name: Unresolved Ambiguity
items.description: In the Mansus, the Hours strive one against another. As the struggles are resolved, they iron out the impossible, exalt the possible, tie the fraying braids of what has been into one golden ribbon of future. Everything is resolved. History becomes the past. There are, however, exceptions. [Exploring with this scrap of knowledge may uncover secret locations in the Rending Mountains, three thousand miles away among the wreck of the oldest empires.]
items.description_cn: 在漫宿中，司辰互相抗衡。纷争平定后，祂们消解了不可能之事，歌颂了可能之事，将纠缠交错的已成之事细密编织成如金色丝带般的未来。万事落定，历史成为过去。然而例外依然存在。[用此知识残篇探索，或可发现撕身山脉中的秘密地点，位于三千英里之外最古老帝国的遗骸之中。]

items.name: Vagabond's Map
items.description: The Vagabond is the one Hour who can never enter the Mansus, but she goes everywhere else... and, if you believe her boasts, she's the only one who knows all the Histories. Sometimes, she lets someone record her travels. [Exploring with this scrap of knowledge may uncover secret locations in the Lone and Level Sands, far from here.]
items.description_cn: 浪游旅人是一位无法踏足漫宿的司辰，但她能前往其他任意地点……并且，如果你相信她的自夸，她还是唯一知晓每重历史的人。有时候，她会让某人记录下她的行踪。[用此知识残篇探索，或可发现遥远的荒寂而平阔的沙地中的秘密地点。]

items.name: Port Noon Anecdote
items.description: Port Noon is where the Long go to enjoy the sea and the sun, to drink from the Spring that makes them forgotten, and to stay out of trouble. Mostly out of trouble. The stories you can hear in the Hotel Ciervo are golden-dewed, quintuple-distilled toasts to memory, served straight up. [Exploring with this scrap of knowledge may uncover secret locations in the Evening Isles, where Port Noon is located, across the great ocean.]
items.description_cn: 午港是长生者享受大海与阳光，饮下泉水被世界遗忘，躲避纷扰，或者说躲避大部分纷扰之处。你能在希耶尔沃旅店听到的故事，就像一杯将回忆五次蒸馏、不加冰块的鸡尾酒。[用此知识残篇探索，或可发现薄暮群屿的秘密地点，位于大洋彼岸的午港之处。]

items.name: A Sexton's Secret
items.description: Certain knowledge, it is said, can be expressed only through the particular quality of a silence. It has been suggested that one can only read such knowledge with one's eyes closed, but only by mischievous commentators. [Use this in a Rite with a corpse and Edge aspect, and the corpse will rise.]
items.description_cn: 据说，某种特定的知识只能通过特定种类的沉默来表达。那些淘气的注释者建议你闭着眼睛阅读这些知识。[将其与尸体以及刃相一同运用于仪式中，可使尸体复生。]

items.name: A White Ceremony
items.description: When I speak it, my lips don't crisp with frost. Each time, this is surprising. [Use this in a Rite with a Heart influence and Byzantine Tinct to summon the Voiceless Dead.]
items.description_cn: 当我说起它时，我的双唇不会因寒冷而结霜。每次都是如此，令人惊讶。[将其与心之影响以及拜占庭染剂一同运用于仪式中，可召唤无声亡者。]

items.name: An Operation of the Declining Sun
items.description: This invokes, acknowledges and welcomes the passage to silence. [Use this in a Rite with a Heart influence and Byzantine Tinct to summon the Voiceless Dead.]
items.description_cn: 唤起、知悉并接纳通往沉默的道路。[将其与心之影响以及“拜占庭染剂”一同运用于仪式中，可召唤无声亡者。]

items.name: Invocation of the Ivory Dove
items.description: There is a power that commemorates and grieves, from whom nothing is taken, but who cannot be deceived. You might expect to be able to crush him in your hand, into bird-bone fragments. [Use this in a Rite with Martensite Paste and an assistant dedicated to Knock - or other resources of equal power - to summon a Maid-in-the-Mirror.]
items.description_cn: 有一位司掌纪念与哀悼的神灵，他已被剥夺至尽，然而他不受欺骗。你或可期待将来能亲手碾碎他，把他变成一把碎鸟骨。[将其与“马氏膏”以及一名追奉启的助手——或其他有着同等力的资源——一同运用于仪式中，可召唤镜中少女。]

items.name: Recitation of Lost Hours
items.description: Six are gone. Five came from Stone and one from Light. All went to Nowhere. Still their memories have power, and now we call upon it. [Use this in a Rite with Martensite Paste and an assistant dedicated to Knock - or other resources of equal power - to summon a Maid-in-the-Mirror.]
items.description_cn: 六位已逝。五位源自岩石，一位源自光。现都归于虚界。但他们的回忆仍具神力，而我们现在要拜请这种神力。[将其与“马氏膏”以及一名追奉启的助手——或其他有着同等力的资源——一同运用于仪式中，可召唤镜中少女。]

items.name: The Divisions of the Names
items.description: When the Sun-in-Splendour was divided, its Names fractured too. Here are the shards of their names which once were whole. [Use this in a Rite with Martensite Paste and an assistant dedicated to Knock - or other resources of equal power - to summon a Maid-in-the-Mirror.]
items.description_cn: 当骄阳被分裂，它的具名者亦随之崩解。这些是曾为整体的那些具名者们的碎片。[将其与“马氏膏”以及一名追奉启的助手——或其他有着同等力的资源——一同运用于仪式中，可召唤镜中少女。]

items.name: Wolf-Word
items.description: When the Forge is cold and the Glory is dark and the Wood is dust, perhaps the Wolf Divided will rest, but only until it can devour itself. This Word almost expresses the Divided One's hatred. [Speak this to a Hunter, and it might drive them insane on the spot.]
items.description_cn: 当铸炉冷却，辉光黯淡，林地化尘，裂分之狼也许方能将息，却止于其能噬己之时。此言几道出了被分裂者的怨恨。[对猎人说出此言，也许能令其当场发疯。]

items.name: Formula: Elixir Zeboim?
items.description: I have here a secret - a recipe of honey, asphodel, powdered ivory, and a mottled fungus that grows only where the dead are buried.
items.description_cn: 我取得了一个秘密配方——蜂蜜、冥府百合、象牙骨粉，再加一种只在埋葬死者处生长的斑点菌菇。

items.name: Formula: Elixir Zeboim
items.description: That formula which quickens the memories of decaying flesh in the bellies of the living. Such a thing could not exist without the consent of both the Flowermaker and the Elegiast... and with the assistance of one more Hour besides.
items.description_cn: 此配方用于复苏处于生人肚中的腐肉的回忆。这种药既然存在，必得到了制花人和悼歌诗人的允许……还有另一位司辰的协助。

items.name: A Thrilling Air
items.description: The senses are sharpened. [A second-order influence: apparent to the perceptive, instantly recognisable to an adept. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions.]
items.description_cn: 五感变得敏锐。[一种二阶影响：对于有洞察力的学徒来说很明显，立刻能被辨别出来。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下。]

items.name: A Rousing Air
items.description: The passions are roused. [A sixth-order influence: the signs are unmistakable. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions.]
items.description_cn: 群情激昂。[一种六阶影响：迹象显著无误。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下。]

items.name: A Furious Air
items.description: Anger is implicit in every shape. [A tenth-order influence! A gathering knot of power and peril. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions.]
items.description_cn: 愤怒以各种形态彰显。[一种十阶影响！力量与危险互相穿插，结为一体。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下。]

items.name: A Resolution
items.description: Who can avert the finality of battle? [A fifteenth-order influence! This might be the personal attention of an Hour. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions.]
items.description_cn: 谁人能将注定的战局扭转？[一种十五阶影响！可能引来某位司辰亲身过问。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下。]

items.name: A Rising Heat
items.description: A haze and a shimmer. [A second-order influence: apparent to the perceptive, instantly recognisable to an adept. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions, and some minions will leave it lingering when they are destroyed.]
items.description_cn: 薄雾与微光。[一种二阶影响：对于有洞察力的学徒来说很明显，立刻能被辨别出来。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下，并且会在某些手下被摧毁时遗留。]

items.name: A Trembling Heat
items.description: The possibility of sparks. [A sixth-order influence: the signs are unmistakable. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions.]
items.description_cn: 迸出火花的可能性。[一种六阶影响：迹象显著无误。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下。]

items.name: An Exalting Heat
items.description: This is the aura at the volcano's edge. [A tenth-order influence! A gathering knot of power and peril. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions.]
items.description_cn: 这是火山的边缘散发出的气息。[一种十阶影响！力量与危险互相穿插，结为一体。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下。]

items.name: An Incandescence
items.description: Change follows fire. [A fifteenth-order influence! This might be the personal attention of an Hour. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions.]
items.description_cn: 改变随火焰而来。[一种十五阶影响！可能引来某位司辰亲身过问。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下。]

items.name: An Awareness of Appetite
items.description: Every sense is heightened; every sensation, deepened. [A second-order influence: apparent to the perceptive, instantly recognisable to an adept. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions, and some minions will leave it lingering when they are destroyed.]
items.description_cn: 所有知觉都被增强；所有感情都被加深。[一种二阶影响：对于有洞察力的学徒来说很明显，立刻能被辨别出来。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下，并且会在某些手下被摧毁时遗留。]

items.name: An Urgency of Appetite
items.description: It is difficult to control oneself. [A sixth-order influence: significant resonances or correspondences. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions.]
items.description_cn: 难以控制自己。[一种六阶影响：可引发强烈的共鸣或同感。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下。]

items.name: An Imperative of Appetite
items.description: The lips ache to savour; the fingers ache to clutch. [A tenth-order influence! A gathering knot of power and peril. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions.]
items.description_cn: 唇舌期盼尝味，十指期盼抓扼。[一种十阶影响！力量与危险互相穿插，结为一体。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下。]

items.name: An Incarnadescence
items.description: The very air is succulent with possibility. Pierce it, and it might bleed. [A fifteenth-order influence! This might be the personal attention of an Hour. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions.]
items.description_cn: 连空气都似果肉饱含汁水般饱含着可能性。刺一下说不定便会淌出。[一种十五阶影响！可能引来某位司辰亲身过问。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下。]

items.name: Trembling Airs
items.description: The toes tap. All is brisk and all is well. [A second-order influence: apparent to the perceptive, instantly recognisable to an adept. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions, and some minions will leave it lingering when they are destroyed.]
items.description_cn: 轻点脚尖。轻快又舒适。[一种二阶影响：对于有洞察力的学徒来说很明显，立刻能被辨别出来。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下，并且会在某些手下被摧毁时遗留。]

items.name: Pulsing Airs
items.description: A rising power; a reassuring energy. [A sixth-order influence: significant resonances or correspondences. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions.]
items.description_cn: 力量上涌，精神鼓舞。[一种六阶影响：可引发强烈的共鸣或同感。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下。]

items.name: Pounding Airs
items.description: The heart moves; the world moves. [A tenth-order influence! A gathering knot of power and peril. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions.]
items.description_cn: 世界随心而动。[一种十阶影响！力量与危险互相穿插，结为一体。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下。]

items.name: An Imminence
items.description: The sky is a drum; the earth is ready for its ecstasy. [A fifteenth-order influence! This might be the personal attention of an Hour. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions.]
items.description_cn: 天空为鼓，大地已经准备好接受它的痴狂。[一种十五阶影响！可能引来某位司辰亲身过问。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下。]

items.name: A Stay of Execution
items.description: All flesh fails. But I've been promised that my flesh will fail a little later. [This is a final insurance against sickness, if no Health remains to you.]
items.description_cn: 肉体皆会衰败。但我得到了保证，我的肉体会衰败得稍晚一点。[此卡是在你没有“健康”时对付生病的最后一道保险。]

items.name: Subtle Flaw
items.description: Laces uncoil -- windows swing open -- locks move as if oiled. [A second-order influence: apparent to the perceptive, instantly recognisable to an adept. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions.]
items.description_cn: 系带解开——窗户外敞——锁像上过油一样转动。[一种二阶影响：对于有洞察力的学徒来说很明显，立刻能辨别出来。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下。]

items.name: Subtle Fracture
items.description: Clouds part -- walls creak -- old wounds ache. [A sixth-order influence: significant resonances or correspondences. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions.]
items.description_cn: 云朵分离——墙壁碾动——旧伤作痛。[一种六阶影响：可引发强烈的共鸣或同感。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下。]

items.name: Subtle Rupture
items.description: Geometry contorts -- doors burst open -- snakes boil from the earth! [A tenth-order influence! A gathering knot of power and peril. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions.]
items.description_cn: 框架扭曲——门扉爆开——蛇群自土中沸腾而出！[一种十阶影响！力量与危险互相穿插，结为一体。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下。]

items.name: Wrong Door
items.description: There is a Door that should not open, and even now its hinges are roused -- [A fifteenth-order influence! This might be the personal attention of an Hour. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions.]
items.description_cn: 那里有一扇不该开启的门，现在连它的合页都在摇摇欲动。[一种十五阶影响！可能引来某位司辰亲身过问。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下。]

items.name: A Consciousness of Radiance
items.description: There is a light behind the world, a light above the Mansus, a light that penetrates both glass and skin. It is present here. [A second-order influence: apparent to the perceptive, instantly recognisable to an adept. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions, and some minions will leave it lingering when they are destroyed.  If unused, it will become Fascination.]
items.description_cn: 在世界背后，有这样一道光，凌驾于漫宿之上，能够刺透玻璃与皮肤。它出现在了这里。[一种二阶影响：对于有洞察力的学徒来说很明显，立刻能被辨别出来。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下，且不会随其中一部分手下的毁灭的而消失。如果不使用，将会拗转为入迷。]

items.name: An Intensity of Radiance
items.description: Light dews the skin and suffuses the air. [A sixth-order influence: significant resonances or correspondences. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions.]
items.description_cn: 光滴落在皮肤上，弥漫在空气中。[一种六阶影响：可引发强烈的共鸣或同感。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下。]

items.name: A Blaze of Radiance
items.description: Every colour has grown bright as new dye, but now all of them begin to bleed towards white. [A tenth-order influence! A gathering knot of power and peril. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions.]
items.description_cn: 每个颜色都更加明亮，仿佛新染过一样，然而现在它们全都开始流失色泽，褪至纯白。[一种十阶影响！力量与危险互相穿插，结为一体。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下。]

items.name: A Splendour
items.description: Cover your eyes, if you like. It will serve no purpose. [A fifteenth-order influence! This might be the personal attention of an Hour. This can be used in some Rites to summon minions.]
items.description_cn: 你可以遮住双眼，随便你。遮也无用。[一种十五阶影响！可能引来某位司辰亲身过问。可用于在某些仪式中召唤手下。]
